MOL-14.title: Introduction to metabolism
objectives: Distinguish catabolism/anabolism and explain ATP/redox coupling.
Locate major pathways and reason about direction and control points.
Connect fed/fasting and stress responses to homeostasis.
Predict upstream, downstream and alternative-route effects of a metabolic block, including PKU.

Control enzyme amount, phosphorylation or an allosteric site
Energy status, homeostasis and fed–fasting transitions
Counter-regulatory hormones: source, trigger and effect
Predict consequences of a pathway block
PKU: apply the block model to phenylalanine

MOL-15.title: Glycolysis I: glucose entry, investment and control
objectives: Compare GLUT1–4 and SGLT and explain insulin-responsive GLUT4 trafficking.
Trace all five investment reactions and distinguish glucose trapping from the committed step.
Compare hexokinase and glucokinase and connect kinetics with tissue function.
Predict PFK-1 responses to cellular energy and insulin/glucagon signals.
Calculate carbon and energy balance for the whole pathway.

topics.title: Glucose transport: gradient, tissue and affinity

MOL-16.title: Glycolysis II: payoff, redox balance and pyruvate fates
objectives: Trace steps6–10 and distinguish NADH formation from direct ATP formation.
Explain pyruvate kinase regulation and red-cell disease.
Compare mitochondrial redox recycling with lactate formation, including oxygenated red cells.
Match each major pyruvate fate with its enzyme and physiological role.
Interpret raised lactate without equating it automatically with hypoxia or metabolic acidosis.

MOL-17.title: Pyruvate oxidation and the TCA cycle
objectives: Explain mitochondrial pyruvate entry and PDH reaction, cofactors and regulation.
Trace all eight TCA reactions, carbon changes and energy-producing steps.
Calculate per-turn and per-glucose outputs using a stated ATP convention.
Explain energy-dependent regulation, indirect oxygen dependence and the dual role of succinate dehydrogenase.
Connect thiamine deficiency, amphibolic withdrawals and pyruvate-carboxylase anaplerosis.

topics.title: Pyruvate entry and irreversible oxidative decarboxylation
PDH components, five cofactors and thiamine deficiency
PDH phosphorylation matches oxidation to demand

Control points and energy-state integration
Succinate dehydrogenase bridges the TCA cycle and ETC
Amphibolic withdrawals and anaplerotic replacement

MOL-18.title: Electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation
objectives: Trace NADH- and succinate-linked electron flow and mobile carriers.
Explain redox reactions and the role of oxygen at Complex IV.
Account for proton pumping, proton-motive force and F₀F₁ ATP synthase.
Compare modern NADH/FAD-linked ATP equivalents under stated assumptions.
Predict inhibitor versus uncoupler effects and explain UCP1 thermogenesis.

MOL-19.title: Gluconeogenesis
objectives: Explain the overlapping transition from dietary glucose to glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
Trace lactate, alanine, glycerol and propionate into glucose production.
Explain the three bypasses, four enzymes, energy cost and compartment requirements.
Predict reciprocal regulation by acetyl-CoA, F2,6BP, insulin/glucagon and the metabolic effect of metformin.

Glycolysisp17Q3 repaired to isolate allostery from hormonal signals.
ETCp16: cyanide is a poison; hydroxocobalamin is an antidote. FDA source linked.
NotesETC16: direct ETC and ATP synthase blockade have different gradient effects.
GNGnotes11: pyruvate kinase is the final glycolytic step, first bypass from pyruvate.
GNGp7 lipid-carbon statement is not a claim that glycerol/odd-chain fats are the main sources of all gluconeogenesis.
